newsitem.title: EGYPT: Hamas says Jerusalem bomb planners want anonymity. [CORRECTED 11:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Hamas says Jerusalem bomb planners want anonymity. [CORRECTED 11:45 GMT]

text.p: The spokesman of the Islamic group Hamas said in remarks published on Wednesday that confusion over who carried out twin suicide bombings in Jerusalem means that its planners do not want to be known.

A leaflet issued in Hamas's name last week claimed responsibility for the attack that killed 15 people, including two bombers, in a west Jerusalem market last Wednesday. Israeli and PLO officials questioned its authenticity.

Hamas spokesman Mahmoud al-Zahar told the Egyptian weekly magazine el-Musawwar in an interview: "This confusion in announcements of claims of responsibility for the incident means that the party that planned and implemented it does not want to announce openly for reasons of its own."
The magazine did not say where or when the meeting with Zahar took place.
Another leaflet in the name of Hamas's military wing said on Tuesday a deadline for Israel to free Palestinian prisoners had expired and promised a chain of attacks inside the Jewish state.
Zahar did not repeat the original Hamas claim of responsibility. But asked if he expected "new operations" as promised unless Israel freed the Palestinian prisoners it held, he told the magazine:

"Israeli prisons hold 4,000 detainees, 250 of which are Hamas and the rest from (Islamic) Jihad and others. The Palestinian street is boiling from peace which has not been achieved, and the embargo on food and on the other hand we have corruption and bribery...What are you waiting for?"
Hamas opposes the interim peace deals that Palestinian President Yasser Arafat signed with Israel as a sell-out of their goal to found an Islamic state in all of Palestine.
Israel closed the West Bank and Gaza after the twin bombing, stopping tens of thousands of Arab workers from reaching their jobs in Israel, paralysing trade and shutting down factories.
Israel has detained more than 170 Palestinians since the attacks.

Palestinians have condemned the Israeli steps as collective punishment and warned Netanyahu that tough sanctions would breed despair, strengthen extremists and weaken Arafat, already under pressure over allegations of corruption in his cabinet.

Zahar said Hamas attacks now focused on civilians rather than the military because Israeli military units took protection inside settlements and had started going out on joint patrols with Palestinian police as part of the Israeli-PLO peace deal.
He said Hamas began to attack civilians after a Jewish settler massacred Palestinian worshippers in a mosque in Hebron in 1994 (corrects year from 1995 to 1994).
"What are Palestinians supposed to do? They kill us and they don't offer condolences," Zahar said.

"The Israeli soldier who opened fire and killed a Palestinian in Hebron is now walking freely through the streets of Tel Aviv without trial or punishment. Israelis must drink the same poison they make us taste," he added.
He was referring to Israeli soldier Noam Friedman's New Year's day attack in a Hebron market in which seven Palestinians were wounded.

An Israeli military court found Friedman unfit for trial and ordered him sent to a psychiatric hospital in February. Hospital officials say he is allowed to spend weekends at home and one day a week studying at a Jewish seminary.
(Adds paragraph to clarify that the Israeli soldier did not kill a Palestinian, as Zahar said, but wounded seven).
